purpose: Mitomycin is used to treat certain types of cancer, including stomach, bladder, and lung cancers. It is also used directly in the bladder to treat early-stage bladder cancer. In some forms, it is used during eye surgery to prevent scar tissue from forming.
how_it_works: Mitomycin works by damaging the DNA inside cancer cells so they cannot grow or multiply. Think of it like putting a wrench in the gears of a cancer cell's copying machine. This helps stop the tumor from getting bigger and spreading to other parts of the body.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, mouth sores, tiredness, and low blood counts (which can increase your risk of infection, bleeding, or anemia). When used in the bladder, you may feel burning or the urge to urinate more often.
warnings: This medication can seriously lower your blood counts, so your doctor will monitor you with regular blood tests. It can cause permanent lung damage or kidney problems in some patients. Tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual bruising, bleeding, fever, shortness of breath, or decreased urination. This drug can be harmful to an unborn baby, so reliable birth control is very important during treatment.
typical_dosing: Dosing depends on the type of cancer being treated and how it is given. When given by IV into a vein, it is usually given every 6 to 8 weeks. When placed directly into the bladder, it may be given once a week for several weeks. Your cancer care team will calculate the exact dose based on your body size and overall health.
